brief: Rabobank splits the 10-year Treasury yield's 2026 rise into two separate drivers. Through Sept 23, the Fed did the work: the FOMC's September hike and hawkish dot plot pushed the risk-neutral yield from 4.09% to 4.43%, taking the 10Y to 4.96% while the term premium fell to 0.57%. A troubled $70 billion 5-year auction on Sept 23 (5.033% yield, a 3.1bp tail, dealers left holding 15.8%) flipped the script: the term premium surged to 0.98% while the risk-neutral yield slipped, pushing the 10Y above 5% to a peak of 5.36%. A TIPS-based split shows the same pattern: real yields rose on war-driven oil prices and a resilient, AI-boosted economy, while breakevens stayed flat near 2.35%, so inflation expectations stayed anchored. Because the latest driver is debt-related, Rabobank argues it won't fully reverse and forecasts the 10Y at 5.20% through year-end, easing only to 5.00% by end-2027. Goldman agrees the Fed explains about 70% of the move but downplays the debt thesis, cites cheap valuation and spent technicals, and targets 4.75% by year-end, though it concedes a loss of AI confidence would send yields sharply lower.
